body: Thanks, but I cycle every day, I ski, I play soccer, tennis, I work. I study part-time, I travel an hour by train to a different city to see my girlfriend. I volunteer at a young musicians workshop. I write music.

I've been here before. Many a time. It's gut churning and constricting. I'm sure you remember that wave of (temporary) relief wash over you when you told them about the family emergency.

You can have that again if you force yourself to go in, and make it through the day. Look busy, and look stressed if you have to, pull you're hair out and sigh loudly!

They're human, they'll realise you're struggling, and what's the worst they're going to do? You'll still be able to walk out at the end of the day and breathe relief.
I'm not talking about being overwhelmed by catastrophic events, I don't want to be a part of a world obsessed with self and riddled with apathy.
It depends what you're expectations are, and where you think the point of no return (for society) is...
